reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify baseline patterns among misclassified instances with external XAI tools to quantify feature importance and detect spurious correlations. This approach ensures both semantic plausibility and statistical significance in identifying shared spurious features that may not be semantically meaningful but have high model attribution.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the mean values of all features across instances 541, 340, and 73 to identify any shared unusual or outlier ranges that might suggest spurious patterns.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features with consistent values or ranges across all three instances that deviate from expected class distributions.

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any of the shared features (e.g., compactness, concavity) exhibit non-intuitive patterns (e.g., high values in benign cases) that could be spurious or correlated with misclassification.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis about which features might be spurious due to non-semantic correlations with class labels.

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP identifies feature importance with game-theoretic consistency, helping detect features with high attribution despite low semantic relevance. Integrated Gradients provide gradient-based attribution, useful for spotting spurious feature influence across instances. Sensitivity analysis quantifies how model predictions change when features are removed, revealing which features drive misclassification without actual class relation.
